title: Hubbard physics with ultracold polar molecules: on-site interaction energies for shielded molecules
authors: Carlin Stewart-Wiese, Joy Dutta, Jeremy M. Hutson
abstract: We explore on-site interaction energies $U$ for pairs of shielded ultracold molecules on the same lattice site. We use 2-dimensional effective potentials appropriate for microwave shielding, which have dipole-dipole character at long range but feature a very large repulsive core when the two molecules come close together. This causes very strong correlation between the motions of two molecules on the same site. We find behavior very different from that for ultracold atoms: in particular, there are states for which $U$ is negative for weak lattices but crosses zero to positive values as the lattice strength increases. This behavior is found for both unbound pairs and 2-body bound states. The latter will give access to previously unexplored types of strongly dipolar Hubbard physics with multiple site occupancy.
summary: This paper calculates the on-site interaction energy for ultracold polar molecules trapped in optical lattices using specialized quantum scattering methods. The key finding is that shielding techniques allow for a tunable interaction regime (U/t) unlike standard atomic systems. This opens the door to studying complex, strongly dipolar Hubbard physics with controlled double occupancy.
main_problem: The study investigates on-site interaction energies (U) for pairs of shielded ultracold polar molecules confined to the same lattice site.
main_result: The interaction energy U exhibits behavior distinct from ultracold atoms, potentially becoming negative at weak lattices and crossing zero as lattice strength increases. This enables exploring dipolar Hubbard physics with multiple site occupancy.
method: The authors use coupled-channel calculations to solve the correlated 2-particle relative motion Schrödinger equation for both bound and unbound states.
model_or_system: The system involves ultracold polar molecules trapped in optical lattices, where interactions are governed by long-range dipole-dipole potentials modified by microwave shielding. The physics is framed within the context of Hubbard models.
key_observables: On-site interaction energy (U), tunneling energy (t), and their ratio U/t.
important_parameters: Shielding fields, lattice strength ($\omega$), Rabi frequency ($\Omega$), dipole moment ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The approach neglects anharmonicity of the confining potential and any extension of Wannier functions into neighboring wells.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates U vs. harmonic frequency $\omega$ for NaCs, showing solid (bound) and dashed (unbound) lines; Figure 2 plots U, t, and U/t versus lattice strength ($\lambda$).
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the correlated two-particle problem by separating relative and center-of-mass motions. It compares results for unbound pairs and 2-body bound states to demonstrate tunable dipolar Hubbard physics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses how strong, controllable dipole interactions in molecular systems can modify fundamental many-body models like the Hubbard model, opening avenues beyond simple atomic approximations.
